title: Rehabilitation after revascularisation surgery: a study to improve recovery
official: Rehabilitation for individuals with chronic limb-threatening ischemia post revascularisation: a co-created feasibility trial (HOPE)
summary:
Background and study aims
Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million people globally and is expected to rise in prevalence in Europe and the UK, as well as internationally, by 50% until 2045. The severity of PAD ranges from intermittent claudication (IC), presenting as exertional pain when walking, to the most severe manifestation, chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), which presents as lower limb rest pain or tissue loss. CLTI represents up to 11% of all PAD (25 million globally), especially in individuals from lower socio-economic backgrounds, those with diabetes and ethnic minorities such as South Asians. 
 
CLTI is associated with high rates of limb loss and mortality, equating to a 50% mortality and amputation rate over two years in recent NHS-wide studies, as well as high costs of care. Those with CTLI require urgent surgery (revascularisation) to restore blood flow to the lower limbs. However, despite revascularisation, individuals with CLTI are still at great risk, with 1- and 3-year mortality ranging up to 50%, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at 42% and 1-and-3-year amputation rates reaching 20%.

People with CLTI have limited or no walking capacity, low levels of fitness, a sedentary lifestyle, and a poor quality of life (QoL). Indeed, poor QoL, low fitness, and frailty are all independent predictors of mortality and morbidity. Furthermore, individuals with CTLI often develop anxiety and depressive disorders post revascularisation. Post surgery and without a secondary prevention strategy, these clinical outcomes will only further decline, leading to dependence on others. Therefore, this population urgently requires evidence-based rehabilitation to stop their physical decline, whilst reducing the risk of mortality or amputation. 

A supervised and home-based exercise and education programme is known to help those with cardiovascular disease after they have had a heart stent or bypass surgery, but no studies have investigated if this also benefits those who have had stents or bypass surgery to help blood flow to the legs. The results of this study will help us to understand if an exercise and education programme is beneficial and if we can improve patient care in the future. This study aims to test the feasibility of a rehabilitation intervention that has been co-created for individuals with CLTI post revascularisation surgery. 
 
Who can participate? 
Patients ≥18 years of age diagnosed with CLTI who have undergone open, endovascular, infra-inguinal, and/or hybrid surgery ≥4 weeks ago but within the last 3 months.
 
What does the study involve?
The study is multi-site, and participants will attend whichever centre is most convenient to them. The study involves taking part in an initial baseline assessment before the commencement of a 12-week rehabilitation programme. The rehabilitation programme involves attending in-person exercise sessions once per week and the completion of a home-based exercise prescription. CLTI education sessions will also be provided bi-weekly. At 12 weeks, a final assessment is required to assess improvements in mobility, health, and quality of life. Finally, participants will be invited to participate in an informal interview about their experience in the programme (optional).  
 
 What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Benefits:
This research project may not offer any direct benefit at the time of participation. If any of the study measurements discover anything abnormal with your health, participants will receive prompt and appropriate medical care and attention.
Participants will be eligible to claim up to £60 reimbursement for travel expenses to and from the intervention site during their time on the study. Participants who complete the main HOPE intervention (12-week programme) will receive a £50 voucher as a “thank you” for taking part. 
 
Risks:
The study mainly involves information gathering and non-invasive measurements. No significant risks to the participants have been identified. Exercise testing carries a very small risk of complication; participants may experience common effects such as breathlessness. Exercising with CLTI may result in some lower leg pain, which is common. Participants may also experience muscle discomfort as a result of exercise. This is a normal response and will be minimised with a thorough warm-up and cool down. To minimise risk, only members of the research team who have had appropriate training and experience will conduct the tests and supervise the exercise intervention. 
 
During the interview, participants may be encouraged to talk about experiences which could be upsetting. However, if this occurs, the study team will stop the recording. If participants wish to discuss anything further, they can discuss with the interviewer, and would be encouraged to chat to a friend, family member or GP. 
 
Where is the study run from?
The Manchester Royal Infirmary (Manchester) and Heartbeat (Preston), UK.
 
When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
Recruitment aims to commence in March 2026, and the study will run until April 2027. Participant involvement in the study will take place for 12-weeks, plus an optional interview following programme completion.  
 
Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), UK.
 
Who is the main contact?
Dr Stefan Birkett, s.birkett@mmu.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rehabilitation programme:
1. > = 18 years of age
2. Diagnosed with CLTI
3. Undergone open, endovascular, infra-inguinal, and/or hybrid surgery > = 4 weeks ago but within the last 3 months   
4. Physically able to take part in the rehabilitation programme
5. Able to consent to study activities, participants’ must be compos mentis and able to understand spoken English

Focus group:
1. Involvement in recruitment for the HOPE study OR delivery of the rehabilitation programme
2. Ability and availability to attend an in-person focus group
Exclusion criteria:
1. Additional surgery pending (including any surgical procedure, not only CLTI-related)
2. Unhealed surgical wounds on the legs or feet
